ei.title: The gene-centric view separates the organism...
ei.subject: 5월_2026 고3 모의고사
ei.lesson: The gene-centric view separates the organism...

fullPassage: The gene-centric view separates the organism from its environment, and in large part, removes agency from the organism. The 'environment' becomes a box within which 'gene-motivated' organisms behave. Thus, it misleadingly partitions 'genetic' from 'environmental' causes, giving primacy to the former. Therefore, altruism is denied because 'in reality' organisms behave to enhance their genes in the 'gene pool' ― and love, hate, desires and other motivations flow through and from genes. With this there can be no creativity. The organism is a prisoner of its genes. This is evidently nonsense because, if there is a prisoner, it must be the genes, locked in the organism and obeying its will. It is the organism as a self-organising entity that has motivation and uses genes in its capacity to act. The word 'organism' has its origins in defining organisms as self-organising beings, going back at least to Immanuel Kant's 1790 Critique of Judgment. The gene-centric view strips the organism of its definitive self.

questions.passage: The gene-centric view (A)[separates / connects] the organism from its environment, and in large part, removes agency from the organism. Therefore, altruism is denied because 'in reality' organisms behave to (B)[weaken / enhance] their genes in the 'gene pool' ― and love, hate, desires and other motivations flow through and from genes. With this there can be no creativity. The organism is a prisoner of its genes. This is evidently nonsense because, if there is a prisoner, it must be the genes, locked in the organism and obeying its will. It is the organism as a self-organising entity that has motivation and uses genes in its capacity to act. The word 'organism' has its origins in defining organisms as self-organising beings, going back at least to Immanuel Kant's 1790 Critique of Judgment. The gene-centric view (C)[strips / grants] the organism of its definitive self.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 중요성, 순서, 또는 지위에서 첫 번째인 상태
det.analysis:

det.tip: primacy = 최우선, 수위. giving primacy to the former에서 '전자에 우선권을 주다'라는 뜻.

questions.passage: It misleadingly partitions 'genetic' from 'environmental' causes, giving primacy to the former. Therefore, altruism is _____(deny).

questions.passage: It is the organism as a self-organising entity that has motivation and uses genes in its capacity _____(act).
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 어형을 바꾸어 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: act → to act (to부정사: in its capacity to act)
det.analysis: in its capacity to act — 행동할 능력에서. 'in one's capacity to V' 구문에서 to부정사 사용.
det.tip: capacity to act: ~할 능력. to부정사가 capacity를 수식.

questions.passage: The gene-centric view separates the organism from its environment, and in large part, removes agency from the organism. The 'environment' becomes a box within which 'gene-motivated' organisms behave. Thus, it misleadingly partitions 'genetic' from 'environmental' causes, giving primacy to the former. Therefore, altruism is denied because 'in reality' organisms behave to enhance their genes in the 'gene pool' ― and love, hate, desires and other motivations flow through and from genes. With this there can be no __________. The organism is a prisoner of its genes. This is evidently nonsense because, if there is a prisoner, it must be the genes, locked in the organism and obeying its will. It is the organism as a self-organising entity that has motivation and uses genes in its capacity to act. The word 'organism' has its origins in defining organisms as self-organising beings, going back at least to Immanuel Kant's 1790 Critique of Judgment. The gene-centric view strips the organism of its definitive self.

③ reproduction: 생식 — 유전자 중심과 무관하지 않지만 문맥 부합하지 않음
④ creativity: 창의성 — 모든 것이 유전자에서 오면 자유로운 창의 불가 ←정답
det.tip: With this there can be no creativity. 모든 동기가 유전자에서 나오면 창의성이 불가능하다.
